title: In distress
hookLine: no god but Allah, the Mighty, the Forbearing, Lord of the Throne (Bukhari)
tomorrow: a thin new moon tonight. what do you say to it?

cards: A crash from the kitchen at night. A smoke alarm going off at two in the morning. A phone call that starts with, are you sitting down?
In moments like that no long prayer comes to mind. The Prophet ﷺ had words for exactly that kind of moment, short enough to say on a staircase.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ibn Abbas reports that in distress he would say: there is no god but Allah, the Mighty, the Forbearing. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the mighty Throne.

teach.b: And it goes on: there is no god but Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the noble Throne. Notice what's missing. There's no request in it at all.
In the worst moment, the line doesn't ask for anything. It says who God is, again and again, until the panic has something solid to stand on.
Mighty, and Forbearing: strong enough to change anything, patient enough to wait with you. That's the thing worth telling someone tonight.
Now the week, line by line. Four phrases at dawn, and a beach of foam: like the sea's foam. Sleep handed back each morning: alive again.
The doorstep, packed and still trusting: I trust him. A mosque's two doors: mercy in, bounty out. A meal you didn't make happen: fed without my power.
Worry ahead and grief behind, named apart: refuge from worry.
And today, words with no asking in them, for when asking is too much: lord of the mighty throne. A week of short lines, small enough to carry anywhere.

how: Muslims say this line in moments of distress or fear, sometimes repeating it until calm returns.

o: a call for others to come and help in danger
words of praise only, said when things go badly wrong
a list of needs said aloud during a disaster

games.q: the week, line by line — tap the pairs.

s: the distress line is a list of requests
it asks for nothing; it names who God is.
Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet ﷺ said it in distress
the line calls God only Mighty, never patient
Mighty and Forbearing together: strong, and patient enough to wait with you.

games.q: a friend's car breaks down on the highway at night and she texts, 'i can't even think what to pray.' which line fits?
o: the full morning remembrances, start to finish.
there is no god but Allah, the Mighty, the Forbearing.
O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty.
games.why: when there's no room for a long prayer, the distress line is short and asks nothing; it names who God is.

practice: Close your eyes and let your shoulders drop. Say the first words slowly, in Arabic or English: la ilaha illallah, there is no god but Allah.
Then stay in the stillness, and each time a worry surfaces, answer it with only that, without arguing.

wordCard.voice: In distress: a line of praise only, no request, said when things go badly wrong. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the mighty Throne.

orig.note: Arabic: the Forbearing, the patient one who doesn't rush.

carryVoice: The line to carry: lord of the mighty throne, because when asking is too much, naming is enough. Ten remembrances in.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 6346 (the words in distress, narrated by Ibn Abbas)
